requirements.title: Record the trade name (Oneota Hive & Balm) with the county recorder
requirements.quote: A person shall not engage in or conduct a business under a trade name ... unless the person first records with the county recorder of the county in which the business is to be conducted a verified statement
requirements.notes: Iowa Code 547.1; the Winneshiek County trade name form must be sworn before a notary, and the county fee page (winneshiekcounty.iowa.gov/departments/recorder/recording-basics-recording-fees) lists Trade Names at $7.00 first page and $5.00 each additional page.

requirements.title: Register the business or a fictitious name with the Iowa Secretary of State
requirements.quote: Sole proprietorships, partnerships and other select business structures are not required to register with the Iowa Secretary of State and would not be available in this dataset.
requirements.notes: A sole proprietor's trade name goes to the county recorder (Iowa Code 547.1); the Secretary of State's fictitious name resolution is for LLCs, corporations and similar entities.

requirements.title: Iowa sales and use tax permit
requirements.quote: Register for a permit if the sale of the tangible personal property, specified digital product, or service is taxable. ... A sales tax permit itself is free of charge.
requirements.notes: Lip balm is taxable (Iowa lists cosmetics as taxable); Decorah's rate is 6% state plus 1% local option, 7% total, per the Department's local option rate table effective July 1, 2026.

requirements.title: Collect Iowa sales tax on honey
requirements.quote: With certain exceptions, food and food ingredients are exempt from Iowa sales tax.
requirements.notes: Plain honey is food and exempt, while the same page lists cosmetics (the lip balm) and candy as taxable, so honey sales alone would not need a permit but the lip balm does.

requirements.title: File Iowa sales tax returns
requirements.quote: Taxpayers that collect less than $1,200 in sales and use tax per year will file returns and pay taxes annually. Taxpayers that collect $1,200 or more in sales and use tax per year will file returns and pay taxes monthly.
requirements.notes: At under $25,000 in total sales this is likely an annual return due January 31 of the following year; tax on online orders follows the Iowa delivery address, and separately itemized delivery charges are not taxable.

requirements.title: Iowa transient merchant license for selling at markets
requirements.quote: The provisions of this chapter shall not be construed to apply to persons selling at wholesale to merchants, ... nor to persons selling their own work or production either by themselves or employees.
requirements.notes: Iowa Code 9C.1(3) exempts people selling their own production, which covers the owner's own honey and lip balm.

requirements.title: City permit or license to run a home-based business
requirements.quote: A city shall not prohibit a no-impact home-based business or otherwise require a person to apply, register, or obtain any permit, license, variance, or other type of prior approval from the city to operate a no-impact home-based business.
requirements.notes: No customers or employees come to the home, so this fits Iowa's no-impact home-based business law; Decorah's own home occupation rules (zoning code 17.16.090) could only be read on a third-party copy, which also says no permit is needed.

requirements.title: Decorah general business, peddler or vendor license
requirements.notes: Searched the city's Forms & Applications page (no business, peddler or vendor license listed) and tried the city code on Municode, which is behind a bot check, so the peddler and transient merchant chapter could not be read.

requirements.title: Decorah rules for keeping beehives inside city limits
requirements.notes: Local news (2017) reports the council legalized hives with a per-parcel hive limit and setbacks, but the current ordinance text on Municode could not be read (bot check) and no city page states the limits or whether a permit is needed.

requirements.title: Winneshiek County zoning or home business permit
requirements.quote: However, such powers shall be exercised only with reference to land and structures located within the county but lying outside of the corporate limits of any city.
requirements.notes: Iowa Code 335.3: the home is inside Decorah city limits, so county zoning does not apply.

requirements.title: Iowa food establishment or food processing plant license for honey
requirements.agency: Iowa Department of Inspections, Appeals, and Licensing (DIAL)
requirements.quote: The premises of a residence in which honey is stored; prepared; packaged, including by placement in a container; labeled; or from which honey is distributed.
requirements.notes: Iowa Code 137F.1 lists this residence among what is not a food establishment and not a food processing plant.

requirements.title: Iowa home food processing establishment license
requirements.agency: Iowa Department of Inspections, Appeals, and Licensing (DIAL)
requirements.quote: Cottage food is exempt from all licensing, permitting, inspection, packaging, and labeling laws of the state if the food is sold and delivered by the producer directly to the consumer, or delivered by mail
requirements.notes: Honey is shelf-stable and sold only direct to consumers in person, at markets and by mail within Iowa, so the $50 home food processing license (Iowa Code 137D) is not needed; lip balm is not food and is outside these food laws.

requirements.title: Iowa cottage food label on honey (preparer contact, ingredients, residential-property statement)
requirements.agency: Iowa Department of Inspections, Appeals, and Licensing (DIAL)
requirements.condition: Only if the honey is sold under the cottage food exemption (Iowa Code 137F.20) rather than the honey-residence exclusion in 137F.1.
requirements.quote: The following statement: “This product was produced at a residential property that is exempt from state licensing and inspection.”
requirements.notes: DIAL lists honey separately from cottage foods, so the cottage food label is the cautious choice rather than a clear requirement.

requirements.title: Iowa farmers market food license for selling honey at markets
requirements.agency: Iowa Department of Inspections, Appeals, and Licensing (DIAL)
requirements.quote: The following products may be sold at a farmers market to consumers without being licensed as a farmers market establishment: ... Honey (Please note: Products containing honey need to be individually evaluated).
requirements.notes: The $150 farmers market license is only for unpackaged foods that need temperature control; individual markets may still have their own vendor rules, which are not government requirements.

requirements.title: Label as honey only if the product is entirely honey
requirements.agency: Iowa Department of Agriculture and Land Stewardship
requirements.quote: No person shall package any liquid or semisolid product or label any such product as honey, imitation honey or honey blend, ... unless the entire product is honey as defined in section 190.1, subsection 4.
requirements.notes: Iowa Code 189.14(2); raw honey from the owner's hives meets this, but flavored or infused honey would not be labeled simply as honey.

requirements.title: Net quantity and maker's name on every package (honey jars and lip balm)
requirements.agency: Iowa Department of Agriculture and Land Stewardship, Weights and Measures Bureau
requirements.quote: All packaged products must be conspicuously marked in the English language in legible letters of not less than eight-point, heavy gothic caps on the principal label with the following items:
requirements.notes: The listed items are the product's name, the quantity by weight, measure or count, and the name and place of business of the maker or seller, with no words like 'about' or 'at least' for quantity.

requirements.title: License and inspection of a commercial scale
requirements.agency: Iowa Department of Agriculture and Land Stewardship, Weights and Measures Bureau
requirements.condition: If a scale is used to sell by weight or to weigh packages filled to a labeled net weight.
requirements.quote: Scales used for packaging products shall meet the accuracy and licensing requirements of the Iowa Weights and Measures regulations.
requirements.notes: The same FAQ says only NTEP-certified scales can be licensed, licenses are annual and expire December 31, and the fee is $9.00 for a 0-500 lb scale; a kitchen scale is not legal for trade.

requirements.title: Register hive locations with the state apiarist (Iowa beecheck registry)
requirements.agency: Iowa Department of Agriculture and Land Stewardship, State Apiarist
requirements.condition: Registration is the way to get the pesticide-applicator protections of the Iowa Bee Rule; the rule ties it to protecting the bees.
requirements.quote: Owners of apiaries, in order to protect their bees from pesticide applications, shall register the location of their apiaries with the state apiarist.
requirements.notes: Iowa Admin. Code 21-45.31(1); registration expires December 31 each year and IDALS describes the registry as a tool to keep bee-toxic spraying away from registered hives.

requirements.title: Entry permit to bring bees or used comb equipment into Iowa
requirements.agency: Iowa Department of Agriculture and Land Stewardship, State Apiarist
requirements.condition: Only if the owner brings colonies, packages or used equipment with combs into Iowa from another state (not packages shipped by the U.S. Postal Service).
requirements.quote: A person who desires to move a colony, package, or used equipment with combs into this state shall apply to the state apiarist for a written entry permit at least sixty days prior to the proposed entry date.
requirements.notes: Iowa Code 160.5(3) exempts packages shipped by the U.S. Postal Service.

requirements.title: Federal honey labeling: call it honey
requirements.quote: If a food contains only honey, the food must be named “honey,” which is its common or usual name (see section 403(i) of the FD&C Act and 21 CFR 101.3(b)).
requirements.notes: FDA's honey guidance also says a single-ingredient honey needs no ingredient statement, and it may name the floral source (for example, Clover Honey).

requirements.title: FDA food facility registration
requirements.quote: For example, farms, retail food establishments and restaurants are exempt from food facility registration requirements, as are private residences where FDA-regulated food is made.
requirements.notes: The honey is produced and packed at a private residence and sold directly to consumers.

requirements.title: Nutrition Facts panel on honey
requirements.quote: Another type of exemption applies to retailers with annual gross sales of not more than $500,000, or with annual gross sales of foods or dietary supplements to consumers of not more than $50,000.
requirements.notes: Under $25,000 in sales qualifies with no notice to FDA, as long as the label makes no nutrient content or health claims.

requirements.title: National Honey Board (USDA honey checkoff) assessment
requirements.agency: USDA Agricultural Marketing Service / National Honey Board
requirements.quote: A first handler who handles less than 250,000 pounds of honey or honey products per calendar year or an importer who imports less than 250,000 pounds of honey or honey products per calendar year is exempt from paying assessments.
requirements.notes: 7 CFR 1212.53(a); a producer who sells directly to consumers counts as the first handler, and a backyard operation is far below 250,000 pounds.

requirements.title: Lip balm label: name and place of business
requirements.quote: The FD&C Act requires cosmetic labels to identify the name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor. By regulation, this includes the street address, city, state, and ZIP code
requirements.notes: FDA says a P.O. box or website is not adequate for this, though the street address may be left off if the business is in a current city or phone directory.

requirements.title: Lip balm label: ingredient declaration
requirements.quote: cosmetic ingredient declarations are required only on the label of the outer container of cosmetics customarily sold at retail or used in the performance of services conducted within the households.
requirements.notes: The lip balm is sold at retail, so it needs an ingredient list in descending order of predominance by common or usual names, along with identity and net contents on the front panel.

requirements.title: Lip balm label: contact for adverse event reports (MoCRA)
requirements.quote: each cosmetic product shall bear a label that includes a domestic address, domestic phone number, or electronic contact information, which may be a website, through which the responsible person can receive adverse event reports
requirements.notes: FD&C Act section 609(a), added by MoCRA; small businesses are not exempt from this label requirement.

requirements.title: Keep records showing the lip balm is safe (MoCRA safety substantiation)
requirements.quote: a manufacturer, packer or distributor whose name appears on the label of a cosmetic product is required to ensure adequate substantiation of safety of their cosmetic product and to maintain records that support substantiation.
requirements.notes: FDA says no specific tests are required and existing safety data on the ingredients can be used.

requirements.title: Report serious adverse events from the lip balm to FDA
requirements.condition: Only if the business learns of a serious adverse event linked to the lip balm.
requirements.quote: A responsible person is required to report serious adverse events associated with the use of cosmetic products in the United States to FDA within 15 business days.
requirements.notes: MoCRA's small business exemptions cover only GMP, registration and listing, so this duty still applies.

requirements.title: FDA cosmetic facility registration and product listing (MoCRA)
requirements.quote: whose average gross annual sales in the U.S. of cosmetic products for the previous 3-year period is less than $1,000,000, adjusted for inflation ... A small business is exempt from the registration and listing requirements.
requirements.notes: Lip balm is not an eye-area, injected, internal-use or long-wear product, so the small business exemption applies; FDA issues no exemption certificate.

requirements.title: FDA cosmetic good manufacturing practice rules (MoCRA)
requirements.quote: MoCRA exempts certain small businesses from GMP, registration, and product listing requirements.
requirements.notes: FDA's page still lists cosmetic GMP regulations as something it must establish, and the small business exemption would cover this owner once they exist.

requirements.title: FDA approval or license to make and sell lip balm
requirements.quote: The law does not require cosmetic products and ingredients, except for color additives, to be approved by FDA before they go on the market.
requirements.notes: The same page says it is not against the law to make cosmetics at home and that FDA does not license cosmetics firms; any added color must be an FDA-approved color additive.

requirements.title: Lip balm regulated as a drug (OTC) because of its claims or SPF
requirements.condition: Only if the lip balm contains sunscreen (SPF) or is marketed to treat or prevent a condition, such as healing chapped lips.
requirements.quote: If a product is intended to affect the way a person’s body works, or to treat or prevent disease, it’s a drug, but sometimes it is both a cosmetic and a drug depending on its claims.
requirements.notes: A plain beeswax lip balm sold to moisturize stays a cosmetic; drug status brings drug labeling and FDA drug establishment registration with no small business exemption.

requirements.title: Iowa state license or registration to make cosmetics at home
requirements.notes: Searched the Iowa Drug, Device, and Cosmetic Act (Code ch. 126), DIAL's food and cottage food pages and IDR's starting-a-business page and found no cosmetic maker license, but no official page states that none is needed.

requirements.title: Ship website orders on time (FTC Mail, Internet, or Telephone Order Rule)
requirements.quote: If you make no shipment statement, you must have a reasonable basis for believing that you can ship within 30 days.
requirements.notes: Applies to website orders; if an order cannot ship on time, the buyer must be asked to consent to the delay.

requirements.title: Report business profit on Form 1040 Schedule C
requirements.quote: Income tax 1040, U.S. Individual Income Tax Return and Schedule C (Form 1040 or 1040-SR), Profit or Loss from Business
requirements.notes: IRS table of forms a sole proprietor may need; the business has no separate federal return.

requirements.title: Federal self-employment tax (Schedule SE)
requirements.condition: If net earnings from self-employment are $400 or more for the year.
requirements.quote: You must pay self-employment tax and file Schedule SE (Form 1040) if either of the following applies. Your net earnings from self-employment (excluding church employee income) were $400 or more.
requirements.notes: Net profit, not gross sales, sets this threshold.

requirements.title: Federal quarterly estimated tax payments
requirements.condition: If the owner expects to owe $1,000 or more in federal tax when the return is filed.
requirements.quote: Individuals, including sole proprietors, partners, and S corporation shareholders, generally have to make estimated tax payments if they expect to owe tax of $1,000 or more when their return is filed.
requirements.notes: Withholding from another job can cover this, so it depends on the owner's whole tax picture.

requirements.title: Iowa individual income tax return (IA 1040)
requirements.condition: If the owner's counted income passes Iowa's filing threshold (for example, more than $9,000 for a single filer under 65).
requirements.quote: You are using filing status single or married filing separately and the total of the lines listed above is more than $9,000. ($24,000 if 65 or older on 12/31/25)
requirements.notes: Business profit is reported on the owner's personal Iowa return; thresholds shown are for tax year 2025 and change yearly.

requirements.title: Iowa estimated income tax payments
requirements.condition: If the owner expects to owe $1,000 or more in Iowa tax on income not subject to withholding (tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2026).
requirements.quote: Taxpayers who estimate they will owe $200 ($1,000 for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2026) or more in tax on income not subject to withholding must pay estimated tax.
requirements.notes: Calendar-year installments are due April 30, June 30, September 30 and January 31.

requirements.title: Federal employer identification number (EIN)
requirements.quote: You do not need a FEIN if... You are a sole proprietor but do not have employees and You do not sell alcohol, firearms or tobacco and You do not need to pay federal excise taxes
requirements.notes: The owner can use a Social Security number; an EIN is optional (some banks ask for one).

requirements.title: Employer registrations (Iowa withholding permit, unemployment insurance, workers' comp)
requirements.agency: Iowa Department of Revenue; Iowa Workforce Development
requirements.quote: Will you have employees? If so, you will need to: Apply for an employer identification number (EIN) with the Internal Revenue Service (IRS).
requirements.notes: The business has no employees, so employer steps apply only if the owner hires.

hard_calls.about: Whether honey needs the Iowa cottage food label
hard_calls.explanation: Iowa Code 137F.1 takes a home where honey is packed, labeled and distributed out of the food establishment and food processing plant definitions, and DIAL's farmers market page lists honey separately from cottage foods. But Iowa Code 137D (home food processing license) has no honey carve-out, so the clean way to stay license-free is the cottage food exemption in 137F.20, which requires its own label (preparer contact, ingredients, 'produced at a residential property' statement). No official page says which route a honey seller uses.

Rule 21-45.31(1), re-adopted effective 1/1/26, says owners 'shall register' their apiaries, but frames it as 'in order to protect their bees from pesticide applications'. IDALS presents the beecheck registry as a protective tool, and Iowa Code chapter 160 has no registration duty for Iowa beekeepers and no penalty for not registering. Treated here as conditional.

hard_calls.about: Decorah city code could not be read from an official source
hard_calls.explanation: Decorah's official site (decorahia.org, not .gov) links its code to Municode, which returned a bot check that was not bypassed. The beekeeping ordinance (reported adopted in December 2017 with hive limits and setbacks), any peddler or vendor license, and the home occupation section 17.16.090 could only be seen in news reports or a third-party zoning copy. The home business answer rests on state law (Iowa Code 414.33), which bars cities from requiring permits for no-impact home businesses.

hard_calls.about: Do backyard hives keep it a 'no-impact' home business?
hard_calls.explanation: Iowa Code 414.33 requires no-impact business activities to 'not be visible from an adjacent property or street'. Hives in a yard may be visible to neighbors. Even if so, the same section makes a home-based business a permitted use subject only to narrow city regulations, and hive placement would be governed by Decorah's beekeeping ordinance (unconfirmed).

hard_calls.about: Scale licensing for filling honey jars
hard_calls.explanation: IDALS says scales used for packaging must be licensed and that kitchen scales are not legal for trade, but its guidance is written for farmers markets. Whether a scale used at home only to fill jars to a printed net weight counts as a commercial device is not spelled out; if the owner fills by volume and never weighs for sale, no license would be needed.

7 CFR 1212.53(a) exempts first handlers under 250,000 pounds a year from assessments, and a direct-to-consumer producer is a first handler. Paragraph (b) says a first handler 'desiring an exemption shall apply' for a certificate of exemption, so it is unclear whether a tiny producer must file anything; treated as not required.

hard_calls.about: Federal labeling reach for sales only within Iowa
hard_calls.explanation: All sales stay in Iowa. FDA's honey and cosmetic labeling rules rest on interstate commerce, and the honey guidance is nonbinding. Iowa's own laws (Code 189.14 honey labeling, weights and measures package labels, Code 126 cosmetics) cover the same ground, so the label items are kept as required.

hard_calls.about: Home street address on the lip balm label
hard_calls.explanation: FDA requires the name and place of business with a street address on cosmetic labels and says a P.O. box or website is not enough, unless the business is listed in a current city or phone directory. For a home business this puts the home address on every product; the MoCRA contact line can be a phone, email or website, but it does not replace the place-of-business line.
